# Templates & examples

Not sure how to start a page? Pick the template that fits, copy it, and
fill in the blanks. You don't need to know Markdown well: the templates show
you what to write and where.

| I want to…                                   | Start from                                          |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Explain how to fix a problem people run into | [Common issue template](common-issue-template.md)   |
| Explain how to do a task, step by step       | [How-to template](how-to-template.md)               |
| See what formatting is available             | [Formatting examples](formatting-examples.md)       |

## How to use a template

1. Open the template page and click the **Edit this page** icon
   (:material-file-edit-outline:) to see its source.
2. Copy everything.
3. In GitHub, go to the right folder under `docs/` (for example
   `docs/common-issues/`) and click **Add file → Create new file**.
4. Name the file with lowercase words and hyphens, ending in `.md`
   (for example `wifi-not-connecting.md`), and paste the template.
5. Replace every placeholder. Delete the grey `<!-- … -->` comment blocks.
6. Add your page to the `nav` section of `mkdocs.yml` so it shows up in the
   menu. Copy an existing line and change the title and file name.
7. Open a pull request (see [How to contribute](../index.md#how-to-contribute)).

!!! danger "Remember: this site is public"

    No passwords and no personal data about students, parents, or staff.
    Say *where* a secret is stored, never the secret itself.
